advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend test_breaching_host_alarms_are_wide_enough_not_to_flap to also assert datapoints_to_alarm is present and < evaluation_periods (not defaulting to a 1-of-N latch) for breaching rebar/host alarms.
evidence: The guard reads only evaluation_periods: `match = re.search(r"^[ \t]*evaluation_periods[ \t]*=[ \t]*(\d+)", masked, re.MULTILINE)` then `if periods < 3:` with no datapoints_to_alarm check
The docstring/assertion itself claims the intended contract is stronger: "Widen to evaluation_periods >= 3 (with datapoints_to_alarm sized below it)" — but 'sized below it' is never asserted
A breaching alarm at evaluation_periods=3/datapoints_to_alarm=1 pages on one absent period, which the ticket names as ordinary timer jitter (~22 of 24 periods present)
advisory.finding: The new guard test_breaching_host_alarms_are_wide_enough_not_to_flap enforces only evaluation_periods>=3 and never checks datapoints_to_alarm, so a future rebar/host alarm at evaluation_periods=3 with datapoints_to_alarm=1 (or unset, defaulting to evaluation_periods) would page on a single absent/jittered period yet still pass the guard — the exact flap failure mode the guard exists to prevent.
scenarios: A new rebar/host alarm added at 300/3/1 under breaching passes the guard but flaps on ordinary probe-timer jitter
advisory.suggested_fix: In the anti-flap test, also parse datapoints_to_alarm from the masked block and flag alarms where it is unset (CloudWatch defaults it to evaluation_periods, which is fine) or where datapoints_to_alarm == 1 while evaluation_periods >= 3 is insufficient to prevent a single-datapoint page.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'publishes unconditionally' rationale on the replication_errors alarm with observability.sh §3, which only publishes when the replication_log file exists (publish 0 when the log is absent, or fix the comment).
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:101 `if [ -f "$REPL_LOG" ]; then` — the entire replication_errors publish (lines 140-142) is inside this guard
monitoring_s5.tf rationale: 'The host probe publishes replication_errors' per-interval delta UNCONDITIONALLY every 5 minutes, so a healthy period publishes 0 — the metric is continuously present.'

REPL_LOG default is `/var/gerrit/site/logs/replication_log` (observability.sh:99); before Gerrit first replicates, or if the path/mount changes, this file is absent and NOTHING is published, so breaching pages on a healthy host
advisory.finding: The replication_errors publish is gated by `if [ -f "$REPL_LOG" ]` (observability.sh §3), so it is NOT published unconditionally as the monitoring_s5.tf rationale now claims; with treat_missing_data="breaching", a missing/renamed/not-yet-created replication_log file makes the S5 alarm read as breaching and page even though the host and probe are healthy.
advisory.suggested_fix: In observability.sh §3, publish replication_errors=0 in an else branch when $REPL_LOG is absent so the metric is genuinely continuous, matching the breaching rationale.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure disk_used_percent is published every run (e.g. publish a sentinel or 0 when df fails) so the gerrit_data_disk_high breaching semantics hold, or narrow the rationale.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:73 `if [ -n "$used_pct" ]; then` guards the disk_used_percent publish (lines 74-76)
monitoring.tf:241 'Missing data means the host-published disk probe stopped; page rather than letting a dying host clear its own data-volume alarm to OK.'

A transient `df` failure yields empty $used_pct and skips the publish for that interval; the 3-period/2-datapoint window absorbs a single such gap, so this is lower-risk than replication_errors but still contradicts the 'continuously present' premise
advisory.finding: The disk_used_percent publish is gated by `if [ -n "$used_pct" ]` (observability.sh §2), so it is not strictly published every run; the gerrit_data_disk_high alarm rationale relies on continuous presence for treat_missing_data="breaching", but a transient df failure (empty used_pct) publishes nothing that interval.

evidence: Added lines in the diff: `else\n  # Could not compare. Report the breaching value rather than staying silent (see above).\n  oos=1` (observability.sh:434-436) and the now-unconditional `aws cloudwatch put-metric-data ... --metric-name mirror_out_of_sync --unit Count --value "$oos"` (observability.sh:442-443)

search of tests/scripts for `put-metric-data` returns `(no matches)` and for `oos` only the exit-code test's in-sync path — ABSENCE: no test drives the fetch-failure branch (empty gerrit_sha or empty github_sha) and asserts mirror_out_of_sync=1 is published

Named violating input: a run where the `git` stub emits nothing for `ls-remote` (or `curl` fails so gerrit_sha is empty) must publish `mirror_out_of_sync --value 1`; nothing verifies the old silent-on-failure regression cannot return
blocking.finding: The mirror_out_of_sync fail-open fix — the diff's core reliability change, where a failed Gerrit/GitHub comparison now publishes mirror_out_of_sync=1 instead of publishing nothing — has no test. The existing shell harness (tests/scripts/test_observability_exit.py) only exercises the in-sync path (oos=0) and never asserts the value published to mirror_out_of_sync.
scenarios: A future refactor of the else-branch reverts to publishing nothing (or publishes 0) on fetch failure, silently restoring the fail-open the ticket set out to fix — no test would catch it
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test in tests/scripts (mirroring test_observability_exit.py's PATH-shim fixture and test_observability_offsets_6a65.py's aws.log capture) that stubs `git` to emit nothing for ls-remote (or `curl` to exit nonzero), runs the script, and asserts the aws log contains a put-metric-data call for mirror_out_of_sync with --value 1; add a companion asserting the in-sync stub publishes value 0.
